Been playing this game during playtest and had my eyes on it since 2022 through YouTube; the development throughout has been incredibly exciting to watch and I still can't wait to see what comes in the future, especially as someone who's been a fan of Killer Bean for a good while now. I give this rating not out of dislike or hate, but rather as a way to provide criticism for the current state of the game (despite my bias and personal enjoyment for it so far; I really enjoy this game but I know that there's still much to improve). For the current state of this early access, there's definitely a LOT of issues: I came across audio issues where I couldn't hear any sound effects or voices (even starting off in the tutorial). I noticed that the volume for all of the options were automatically set to 0, but even after adjusting it still seemed inconsistent, mainly in the tutorial (this has probably been hotfixed by now). Also, minor nitpick but it would be nice to have some background music throughout the game. As far as the actual gameplay itself, I think the combat has potential but it does feel unpolished; the sliding doesn't actually feel like a slide as the speed is the same as when you run and there's no real sense of momentum, so it feels weird being able to just spam slide the entire time with no consequences or strategy to it. The game also feels a bit TOO easy with the enemies either being completely avoidable (even after confrontation) and dying fairly quick. To add onto this, the finishers are very easy to land so you're able to cheese the fights by simply stunning the enemies and getting all of your health, ammo and dramatic points back. There is the stat multiplier adjustment in settings to make enemies more durable as well as having them deal more damage, but most people may not be aware of the option since it isn't mentioned anywhere in-game and it's more artificial than anything. On that topic, the missions do feel kind of repetitive as most of the objectives are just hacking through several systems, taking down some enemies, grabbing the item, then leaving. And some of the objectives do feel vague and you're typically left to figure stuff out on your own without much of an idea on what to do. I also do think the capture the flag sections could be fixed to indicate whether an area has been captured since it doesn't clearly indicate when you're done. The shop function also feels a little clunky as every mission complete will take you back to the city (even though you're traveling through islands) and you have to inconveniently drive your way there just to make some quick purchases. I do really like the idea of roguelike elements within a game like this, especially since the procedural weapon system is one of the big focuses of the combat, but it doesn't feel like I had the chance to feel its impact, you could most likely end up going the whole game without purchasing a single upgrade. I've listed a lot of flaws in this early access so far but that does not mean that I disliked the game, honestly its the opposite; I see a lot of potential for the game especially since there's plans for multiplayer as well as a randomized campaign, and there's already a lot of charm even from what I've experienced so far (incredibly happy to see the return of the cheesy one-liners + dialogue and of course the ragdoll physics are everything). Despite being unpolished, it's still very satisfying to see this game published, especially considering that this is essentially a one-man passion project. I would say that it may be best to wait until you buy the game, but I admire Killer Bean as a franchise and find Jeff Lew to be an inspiring creator, so I absolutely plan on supporting this game moving forward and definitely keeping an eye out for more updates!

Good game. As for the bad reviews- this is an early access game made by ONE PERSON. You should be a little more forgiving. The most common issue stated is the audio one- no audio. The settings are just set to 0 by default, which Jeff is fixing. The campaign is fully playable, but currently not complete. Multiplayer is also an upcoming feature. A lot of the stuff promised is not yet here, but is planned. Do not purchase expecting immediate completion, but even so, I recommend it, especially given the discount. My only complaint is that the game feels too easy. Only the Jetski section is particularly difficult. I feel like the bosses could have a bit more HP on harder difficulties. The Roguelike elements normally take place in findable weapons and the shop. All in all, solid game.

I'm straight up beaning it. Jokes aside, after around two years of waiting for this game's release, we got what I would like to call the base skeleton of what the game promises to be for future updates in future months, if it does happen if the project does continue, or is forgotten for some reason. After spending 2.6 playing around, messing with the settings, and seeing what it has to offer after like 4 to 5 missions?, There is definitely many areas that the game needs heavy polish. This are some issues I found while messing around: - Default Audio settings upon loading for the first time set at 0% - Inconsistent audio levels with sounds, such as explosions, killing beans, and weapons. - Dialogue tends to not play audio every once in a while. - Animations can sometimes break, unsure of how I could describe the ways you could replicate these animation issues yourself, but if you play around, you can see what I mean. (Some include common weapons not having proper reloads, and sometimes in First Person, you can be holding the Twin Dragon Pistols while also the pickable weapon, thought this is a visual bug) - Default camera sensitivity is very low. Thought this is a player's preference to change it to what you want. - Some weapons don't have ADS sensitivity when aiming, while some do. (There is also no setting to change ADS Sensitivity) - Uhh... I think that's all I can remember as of now, I'll update this if I remember some more, or find more. Outside of that, the game does feel repetitive after three missions. You go to an island, shoot some dudes, hack some things to hear the same dialogue to get info on your map (which the game doesn't tell you, but press TAB to access the map and some other info), and so on. This is saying it from someone who enjoys RPGs and has played some Roguelikes before. If you're into this type of pain, you don't mind the bugs and glitches, and want to shoot some beans to see them ragdoll and be John Killer Bean, then this one's for you. If you're reading this before purchase, and you're considering playing to truly become The Killer Bean, I recommend getting it when it gets on sale, as its currently still unpolished as of writing this. (This is my first time writing an extensive review for a game's release rather than just leaving a funny comment, I hope this information does serve you well if you're considering becoming John Killer Bean) [If only there was a recommendation that's between Yes and No, I would recommend this game in between, but for now, I will leave a positive review, as I did have some fun]

I really wanted to like this game; I really did. I kept missing all the playtests, so when I bought it earlier, it was the first time I ever played this game. All the trailers made it look very good, so the game itself must be good, right? Well, let's start with the positives. Even though the map design leaves much to be desired, the game does look pretty good all things considered. The music is nice and the voice acting is decent, although it won't take too long for Killer Bean to run out of lines during gameplay. To my knowledge this game is being developed by just one guy, which is very commendable. But unfortunately that's it for the positives. The core combat is horrible but barely held together by the ability meter. And when you have abilities, it's sort of fun. But in the downtime where you don't have abilities, it's just unbearable. Most of my issues with the combat would be solved if it were any easier to get health and ability back, mostly health. Unless you get a gun that gives you health off of kills, there is literally no way to heal yourself during combat outside of slow-motion kills and takedowns. Outside of combat, you can find health pickups, though. Melee, within itself, is already very finicky regardless of the target unless you stealthily approach them from the back. If you try to melee a bean during a fight, they and their friends will just shoot/damage you so much that whatever health you'll gain from the takedown won't matter; it's even like this with the melee enemies. You can at least get 10 units of health regenerated after waiting a minute or two. This is only if you have under 10 health. The maps are huge and vast with not much to actually do in them except get from point A to point B. Yes, there's some computer hacking thing you can do in order to find resources, but it's still boring. The shop between missions is nice since you can buy guns, upgrades, and gun attachments there. If only the gunplay didn't also suck. The first-person mode is just there so they can say there's a first-person mode, since it's pretty much unplayable this way. You go into first person when aiming down sights with most guns, but it's not as bad as just first-person. I want to say that since this is an early access game, there's still time for the game to improve, but to me, it seems like the game is like this at its core. If you want a good finished game based off a web series, just play MADNESS: Project Nexus.

At this moment of the game, I cannot recommend it unless you want to support the dev. The game's current state feels more like a proof of concept rather than an actual, playable game. I played about 5 missions and realized that I would rather get my money back than finish it out. Ultimately, game needs more time in the oven and I hope that it gets that in the future. In the meantime, I'll just watch it from afar. I want this game to be good, and I hope it gets the love that it deserves.

I'm conflicted. Look, Killer Bean Forever 4K - Official FULL MOVIE is a cinematic masterpiece. There's no denying that. The fact that it was made by a single person is seriously impressive. It's been a staple of internet and meme culture for a long time, and with good reason. This Killer Bean game, on the other hand, not so much. I get it. Jeff Lew still wants to be a one-man prodigy for this franchise. But it turns out that designing and making engaging video games is really, really frickin' hard. Killer Bean is not yet an engaging video game. While the core feeling of controlling Killer Bean is fun on the surface, the gameplay loop is severely lacking. The "campaign" is a series of disconnected missions that have you running around dispatching cannon fodder, capturing objectives, and holding "E" on devices scattered throughout poorly designed maps. The roguelite elements amount to meaningless stat upgrades that have little to no impact on gameplay. The other game modes are basically the same thing, just with less content. What *Killer Bean* does have is Jeff Lew's DNA for animation and spectacle. The special abilities—bullet time, throwing a bullet into the air and shooting it to hit someone out of sight, the breakdance ultimate move—are all great fun. I kind of wish he had focused more on the things he's already proven himself to be really good at: spectacle and humor. Because based on this game, I'm not convinced Jeff understands game design in a broader sense. Just throwing ideas together because they look cool doesn't make for a compelling video game. Sure, it's an Early Access game. These things are subject to change. But this game has also been five years (or more) in the making. It was initially slated for release in 2024. Unless something fundamentally changes in the way Jeff structures the design pillars of this game, or he hires someone to help him sort them out, I have doubts that Killer Bean will ever reach its potential. I hope to be proven wrong.

I feel people have been a bit too unfair to this game, THIS IS AN EARLY ACCESS!!! I want to clarify beforehand that I've been playing it since the playtest and I do have a few comments on the current state of the game though - New missions, bosses and music/voice acting aside, this is barely any different from one of the last builds I could try from the playtest. I think Jeff rushed this release a bit too much, I even find it weird how there was nearly no announcement done for it, beside some social media posts and YouTube Shorts. - Many bugs are still present (I got clipped into some buildings and stuck after getting up from explosions quite a few times, for example). I'm not really sure when a voiceline is meant to play or not, because not every dialogue is voiced as you would expect. Some lines are silent and then immediately after the character does voice the next line. Many text boxes are way too short as well, the characters are still talking and the text box is already over, and the list goes on, but I don't want to stuff this part too much. Not every issue is critical, but it definitely undermines a lot the experience and gives a REALLY BAD impression of the game for a paid release - I think the difficulty is just fine as someone who does NOT play shooter games often, I feel the enemies have a fair reaction time for you to shoot them and sometimes they have a pretty accurate precision... hence the sometimes, it's a very coin flip kind of thing. As long as you don't abuse the breakdance ability or play overly cautious (like killing everything off their range) the game should remain fairly challenging, especially because the challenge is based on "wave control" rather than one-on-one combats, not counting the mini/bosses of course. - The whole thing with the city definitely feels... weird, I don't know how to explain it. It feels so dead and empty. I believe people call these "liminal spaces". As someone who likes to wander around and explore for no reason, I find it interesting to explore those places even if there is nothing to do. I think It would be cool to have extra objectives every time you revisit the city, that would bring a purpose to those places. Something like side-quests that allow you to "clear the trash" off the city to unlock stuff. I miss the accessible hospital :( I think that's all I can think of for the moment. I really hope Jeff is reading these reviews and will consider the feedback to improve the game. I personally enjoy it and hope everybody can do it as well in the near future. Now that it is on sale he can get a LOT MORE insight on what the players think and want for the game. Please continue building this up to perfection! Don't let the negative reviews discourage you!

[h1]I cannot recommend this game in its current state.[/h1] [h3]Only buy this game if you’re interested in helping Jeff Lew make it. It’s very rough right now.[/h3] I’ve been a big fan of Jeff Lew’s work for years now. I’ve always loved the janky, indie feel of Killer Bean. I love the short films and the subsequent film (KBF is an unironically good movie, fight me). All of these jank here is not quirky, it’s slop-level jank. This game is just bad in its current state. I’ve been part of the play tests for a while, and this Early Access release is not much different. This game was not ready to release. I understand that Jeff is the sole developer, but this game is bordering on asset flip. It’s fun at times, but that’s ruined by the extremely poor optimization and sheer amount of bugs, softlocks, and the odd save system (my campaign progress doesn’t save, but the weapons I had do). The game just feels empty and is extremely barebones. I have been anticipating this game ever since it was announced and am disappointed with the product as of EA release. I look forward to see necessary changes being implemented. This game can be good. Right now, it’s just not. Jeff, I hope you don’t give up, this could be a good game, and I appreciate your dedication to staying solo, but [i]please[/i] consider hiring some experienced developers to help you. It could only do good for the game and will help you become a better developer yourself!

The Killer Bean game is finally out after years of waiting, and after giving it some days, it has amazing potential. Many dislikes gave this game a mixed review but only 3 days have passed and Jeff has patched so many bugs and added many more features. A lot of people don't realize that this entire game was made by one person, and you can complain that the game was bad on its first day, but it's still in early access and is constantly being worked on. Yes, there are still many bugs and bad game designs sprinkled throughout the game, but the game is still workable. By the rate Jeff works on the game, by the end of the year we might have bean customization, a full city to work with, better animations for first/third person, and a bug-free experience. For the people who are not recommending the game, your opinion is acceptable, especially in the games current state along with its somewhat high price, but we should be lucky Jeff allowed us to play the game as it is. As long as we stay patient, Killer Bean can become 2026's GTA VI.

Honestly, I wanted to love this because the third-person movement and fighting mechanics are incredibly smooth. But the rest of the game feels half-baked Here is everything currently broken or missing: * **Wobbly first-person:** Mechanics feel great until you switch to first-person, which is super wobbly. * **Exploding RPG:** The RPG literally explodes in your face the second you pick it up. * **Vanish objectives:** Glitches cause objectives to disappear, forcing a total mission restart. * **"Gun Name":** Some weapons are literally labeled "gun name" with zero stats. * **Choppy audio:** Voice lines constantly cut in and out. * **Lives system:** It adds nothing but frustration and honestly just needs to be removed. * **Unpolished graphics:** The visual department needs a massive amount of polish. * **Grey screen glitch:** The low-health grey filter frequently gets stuck on screen even after healing. * **Zombie glitch:** A bug at 0 health leaves you unable to move but still able to shoot. * **Stuck animations:** Character gets locked in a running animation or glides around without moving their legs. * **Broken jumping:** Random movement bugs completely break your ability to move or jump right. * **Super mech culprit:** The last three glitches are almost certainly caused by using the grenade launcher inside the super mech mission. * **Zero story:** No explanation for why Killer Bean hates the shadow beans, and there's no ending cutscene. Beating the final boss feels like you just killed a random drone and the game gave up. * **Missing trailer content:** The trailers hyped up piloting a jet, a missile helicopter, and a teleporting sword-fight boss, but none of it is actually in the game. It has potential, but wait for a few major patches before buying.

Considering the constraints and repeated delays this game has had, I'm having a lot of fun with it. It's clearly unfinished and rough around the edges, but not to the point of unplayability. At this point I played almost 24 hours and none of it has felt boring. The singleplayer campaign is relatively short, but it doesn't lack replay value. Many elements are procedurally generated at the start of the campaign, which makes every run a little different. You can switch up the difficulty for more challenge, and go between first and third person views. It picks up the story of Killer Bean after the short lived series and 2008 movie. The mechanics and cutscenes are all pretty barebones right now, but it works for now and more seems to be planned in the future. Killer Bean and NPCs talk a lot during gameplay and combat. I find the excessive talking charming and matching the game's tone, but they can be turned off if you don't like it. The game nails the ragdoll physics and KB's signature moves like the bullet time and break dancing. The acrobatics/parkour system wasn't super hard to pick up, honestly feels a bit like COD: Advanced Warfare's exo-suit jumping. The game modes outside of the campaign are worth playing too. Conquest is your basic Player vs NPC capture the flag mode and likely models what a future multiplayer mode could look like. Dance Party is five rounds of progressively bigger warehouse dance parties that Killer Bean needs to shut down, calling back to the first scene of the movie. Battle Arena is an endless wave survival game mode, and the one I've put the most hours into trying to get a high round (22 so far). These share certain procedurally generated elements with the campaign It's not without its rough spots, there have been certain bugs that have required me to restart or return to the main menu. It's also three weeks old early access, so I ain't gonna dunk on it hard for that. It feels a bit like playing a 2007 PC game. But the team is releasing weekly updates and listening to feedback in the discussions so they identify issues as they come up. I'm excited to see what the game looks like in a few months after some polishing and updates. I don't understand the people who play a three week old early access release with a dev team of like 6 people for an hour or less, then call it bad because it feels "unfinished" and "broken". They gotta go back to Warzone

Very few games can really carry the title of "indie" with dignity, integrity and grace. But not only that, but the creator of Killer Bean, the movies and the game, has a commitment that few artists in his craft genuinely have. For that reason, it is hard to say anything negative about a game that celebrates everything joyful about the interactive medium. Yes, there are many things that would be unforgivable in a larger title with a larger IP. The game is crushingly hard, relentlessly unfair at times and relies a lot on trial and error, even with very adjustable difficulty scales and some surprising leniency compared to its more rogue-like initial incarnation. Many mechanics may seem underbaked and there is surely a lot of gameplay burdens inherent to the engine and the fact its mostly done by the hands of a single man. But what is it about Killer Bean that allows us to overlook these genuine flaws? Killer Bean, throughout its history, as a character and an indie IP, really has stood the test of time and acts as a testimonial to dedication in bringing something silly, but inspired to the ever cruel and judgement audience of the internet. The fact the game exists, it is playable and it has more content than most Early Access games, is proof that Killer Bean is more than just an idea, more than just a passion project by a lone man who wanted to share it with the world. When you think about it, Killer Bean is all of us. The aspiration to embrace tropes, whether they be cringe or silly or over done, in full fisted parody and endorsement for "fun above all". Killer Bean is a relentless embrace of a genre oversaturated with silliness. In its core, its enduring and light with impressive cinematic gravity. What it lacks, it actually gains. By discarding a deeper narrative, it can focus on humour. By unironically emulating Call of Duty Warzone, it in term, is a competent parody of it. By being Killer Bean, it allows itself to be a bit of everything, but mostly, unapologetically, itself. Killer Bean is in a language we all understand.

After a LONG wait the Killer Bean game has finally entered early access, so of course I immediately had to grab it. Killer Bean the film is a cult classic because of its surprisingly good action despite the cheesy premise and plot, so I was excited to see how the game worked. First off, the combat. The combat is nothing too special, but I did enjoy it once I figured out all the moves. Dodging feels fluid, the gunplay is... alright, and there's a decent weapon variety. Melee is encouraged due to the lucrative healing it provides - almost too much healing honestly, so I'm glad I only realised you could do it later in the campaign. The levels are pretty meh at the start of the game, being fairly basic and boring, but the late-game has a lot more varied and interesting stages, with the grand finale being a pretty great spectacle where you scale a giant mech and have to survive. It's definitely stronger in the second half. The bossfights of the campaign also feel like this, with the first one being a pretty basic shootout, the second having annoying gimmicks, but the final 3 being pretty great; the penultimate level contains a bullet hell boss with some surprisingly well thought out and enjoyable patterns. I think the earlier levels could be easily improved by adding a lot more dynamic things such as turrets you could control, or more explosive barrels/environmental hazards, or more vehicles. The biggest issue with the game is jank. There are a LOT of bugs; if this was a full release it'd be pretty bad, but since it's early access it's forgiveable. I also have to be honest, a lot of them feel pretty fitting for Killer Bean. My other most notable issue is the spin move; it's a great way to escape a bad situation and regain health, but it's SUCH a slow cutscene every time (other than when used on zombies). I think it'd be good to only do the cutscene shots in HUGE enemy hordes (every few enemies or so), or to fully remove that and make it a move that the player activates and then has to click to fire but gets to be invincible for a bit, making the game keep you engaged. Another issue is the awkward level transitions. Levels just kind of... end, even cutting off dialogue, and you go to the next one; it's really awkward having the screen suddenly blur. Even the campaign just sort of... ends... with no story resolution, which I'm not really sure if it's setup for a sequel or just because it's early access. Also, cutscenes are SOOO slow and unskippable! I didn't mind but it makes replays or loading back into a level SUCH a chore. The game also comes with 3 side modes: The Party, Battle Arena and Conquest. The Party is a 5 stage roguelike where you go through several recreations of the opening party scene from Killer Bean; this is easily the most iconic scene so it's definitely a good thing this is in the game, and the arenas are pretty fun and also stressful and it's a relatively short mode. Also, it has an actual level ending animation and transition, which is an improvement over the main campaign. Battle Arena is just your standard arena mode where you fight waves of enemies, pretty good if you want more, not much else to say. Conquest is a mode where you can fight alongside many friendly NPCs to take control of an island vs an army of enemies; it feels like the war mods for GMod which was pretty nostalgic for me and it's very customisable so there's a lot of fun to be had. It DOES feel like it should be multiplayer but it works singleplayer too and has no issues so it's a fun addition. All in all while it may not be the best game ever I think this is definitely a solid grab if you're a Killer Bean fan, and you will enjoy the roughly 3-4 hours of gameplay it provides. If you're not a Killer Bean fan it might be a harder sell, and I'm not entirely sure if I'd recommend it. I can easily see this game improving over time if Lew puts more work into it though, and it's an admirable effort for a solo dev - definitely early access, but the full release could end up being pretty great! 6/10.
